clue.text: Unexpectedly fresh version of The Great Pretender?

definitions.text: Unexpectedly fresh version of The Great Pretender?

parts.words: Unexpectedly fresh version of The Great Pretender?
parts.note: someone who has shot up unexpectedly and is cheeky (fresh) is cast as a pretender to status, playing on the old song title

explanation.surface: A music fan hears a surprising new cover of an old hit song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version' suggests an anagram or a cover record, but nothing is rearranged: the whole clue describes a brash social climber, who is both 'fresh' (cheeky) and a pretender.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person who has risen suddenly in rank and behaves presumptuously, a pretender to standing.

clue.text: Incompatible girl left Isaac

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Ike is a pet form of the name Isaac

explanation.surface: A girl walked out on Isaac because they were not suited.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are dissimilar in kind may be unable to go together, hence incompatible.

clue.text: Plan to up production of super pies

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells us to read the whole run of letters from bottom to top

parts.note: mega is slang for super, excellent
tarts are open pies

explanation.surface: A bakery decides to increase its output of excellent pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MEGATARTS round to give the answer; 'to' and 'production of' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse devised to achieve an end.

clue.text: Wolf seen in Lakeland

indicators.note: the letters wanted are on view inside the single word Lakeland

explanation.surface: Someone reports a wolf sighting in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District of north-west England. Akela is the wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's Jungle Book, and the name of a Cub Scout leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's Jungle Book the leader of the wolf pack bears this name.

clue.text: Newspaper to run holiday home

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, the very one carrying this puzzle
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A newspaper decides to operate a holiday property.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a holiday property owned jointly, each owner using it for set weeks of the year.

clue.text: Bath — what bus runs there?

indicators.note: something that runs is set loose and its parts move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in Bath asks which bus goes to their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English city with a bus route, but it is the definition, a tub for washing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for washing clothes is a kind of bath.

clue.text: Best of the pits

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to defeat them
slang for the very lowest quality, the least good of all

explanation.surface: A remark that the finest of the coal mines is still awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' and 'worst' look like opposites, but as verbs both mean to beat an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to get the better of, and as an adjective it means of the lowest quality.

clue.text: In this fashion a poet joins artist to produce TV programme

parts.note: so means in this way or manner
Alexander Pope was an English poet
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A poet teams up with a painter to make a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' and 'to produce' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial drama on television about everyday lives, originally sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: A way to replace middle of the sample

indicators.note: the central letter of the word 'the' is swapped out for the preceding pieces

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests a different method of testing a product.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of THE is H; putting A and ST in its place gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a small portion of it, sample it.

clue.text: Scholar raised voice --"Sir!"

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate or scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it to read upwards

parts.note: a tenor is a singing voice

explanation.surface: An academic raises their voice to address someone respectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TENOR into RONET under BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary title and is addressed as Sir, so the title stands for the holder.

clue.text: A lake in an inaccessible place

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A remote lake hidden in hard-to-reach country.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a cliff, a lofty spot hard to reach.

clue.text: Diver's given answer during amalgamation of companies

indicators.note: one piece occurs within the span of another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a merger is the joining of two companies

explanation.surface: A deep-sea diver is given the answer while firms are combining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a person, but it is a diving duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating duck that dives for its prey.

clue.text: En route, stubborn general is ignored

indicators.note: the part named 'general' is disregarded, so it is left out of the longer word

parts.note: intransigent means unwilling to compromise

explanation.surface: On the way, an obstinate army general is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in transit is travelling, on its way between places.

clue.text: Where canoe can come to grief

definitions.text: Where canoe can come to grief

indicators.note: a word that comes to grief is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A warning about the place where a small boat might capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link; the whole clue doubles as definition, since the open sea is where a canoe might founder.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is a body of water where a small boat is at risk of being wrecked.

clue.text: At the finish, the thoroughbred trailing the field moved slowly

indicators.note: the finishing letter of each of the following five words is taken

explanation.surface: A horse race report says the thoroughbred at the back of the field came home sluggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the finish' sounds like the end of a race, but it takes the final letter of 'the thoroughbred trailing the field'.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to advance gradually and carefully, a little at a time.

clue.text: Misuse of this could result in bad credit

definitions.text: Misuse of this could result in bad credit

indicators.note: misusing something puts it to the wrong purpose, so these letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A warning that careless use of plastic can ruin your credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs both ways: misusing the letters of the answer gives 'bad credit', and misusing the card itself can too.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspending on a payment card drawing on your bank account can leave you overdrawn with a poor credit record.

clue.text: One who took the lead, going for gold?

definitions.text: One who took the lead, going for gold?

parts.words: One who took the lead, going for gold?
parts.note: read as a sporting front-runner chasing a medal, it means someone who tried to transmute the metal lead into gold

explanation.surface: An athlete hit the front in pursuit of a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took the lead' and 'going for gold' suggest a race; here lead is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners of a proto-science sought to turn base metals such as lead into gold.

clue.text: Man bearing English flag of inferior quality

indicators.note: a man bearing something carries it within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
a jack is a flag, as in the Union Jack

explanation.surface: A man carries a cheap English flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapjack goods are shoddy and cheaply made, like a pedlar's wares.

clue.text: Where noodles might be having problems

definitions.meaning: noodles are served in a broth
an idiom for being in trouble

explanation.surface: A diner wonders where the noodles have got to while things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the location of noodles in broth, and idiomatically being in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Part of speech I am withdrawing look around for the note

indicators.note: the word for look goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: something withdrawing goes backwards, so these pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A speaker pauses mid-speech and glances round for their notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' sounds like a fragment of a talk, but it is a grammatical class; 'withdrawing' reverses it with I'm to give MIBREV, and 'around' puts the look word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a musical note lasting four beats, the whole note.

clue.text: Set in motion food and drink outside

indicators.note: the word for drink sits outside the food word, around it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a tart is a sweet or savoury pastry

explanation.surface: Picnickers start their meal with food and drink outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up an engine or venture is to get it going.

clue.text: Feature of church required reform, so they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard spoken, so the word sounds like the one we enter

parts.note: to alter something is to change or reform it

explanation.surface: A church feature reportedly needed reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table at the east end of a church is its focal feature.

clue.text: Having entered Mum and Dad mostly raced fast

indicators.note: the parent pieces have gone into the word for raced, so they sit inside it

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, raced
ma is a familiar word for mum

indicators.note: most of the word Dad is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: dad, taken as written

explanation.surface: A child races in after Mum and Dad have gone through the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'raced fast' but is the definition, a noun: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month during which believers abstain from food from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Stop putting sulphur in a container

indicators.note: the sulphur symbol is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemist halts before adding sulphur to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command meaning stop or cease.

clue.text: Shock a parish priest with a lie? That's unacceptable

indicators.note: what is unacceptable is rejected, so the letters named are thrown out of the word lie

parts.note: lie, taken as written
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A parish priest caught telling a lie scandalises everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's unacceptable' looks like a comment on the lie, but IE (that is) is unacceptable, so it is removed from LIE to leave L.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill someone with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Pampered, I become animated? Some hope!

indicators.note: letters that become lively and move about change places

explanation.surface: A spoilt person dreams of starring in a cartoon, with little chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle fantasy that will never happen, as the exclamation 'some hope!' scoffs.

clue.text: Geographical feature, island, covered by map

indicators.note: the island letter is enclosed by the word for map

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A map shows a landform and an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is a broad area of flat land, a landform.

clue.text: Sketched river in early light?

indicators.note: the river abbreviation is placed within the word for early light

parts.note: dawn is the first light of day

explanation.surface: An artist drew a river at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn is the past tense of draw, to make a picture in pencil.

clue.text: Boss has the best fruit

definitions.meaning: a playful literal reading: the finest of yellow fruit

explanation.surface: The manager keeps the finest fruit for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for the chief, and literally the foremost of a yellow fruit.

clue.text: U-turn made by couple nearing American city — not silently

indicators.note: the pieces turn right round, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a duo is a pair
LA stands for Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A couple make a U-turn as they near an American city, loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turn made by' reverses the whole run DUOLA; 'nearing' merely sets the city beside the couple, and the dash hides that 'not silently' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking aloud means voicing words audibly rather than in silence.

clue.text: Young man in agony becomes champion

indicators.note: the young man goes within the word for agony

parts.note: pain is agony
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A youth in torment turns into a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence a heroic defender of a cause.

clue.text: 25 made family doctor popular

parts.note: kin are relatives
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Family and doctor made someone popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 across, meaning boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in an organisation, its chief.
